newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi close to signing Iraq oil deal - sources.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi close to signing Iraq oil deal - sources.

text.p: Mitsubishi Corp is due to sign an agreement to buy around 40,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of Iraqi crude oil, possibly as soon as Friday, industry sources close to the negotiations told Reuters.
"We've heard that an agreement will be signed shortly -- by the end of today," one source told Reuters.
He said the total volume being discussed by Mitsubishi representatives in Baghdad was 40,000 bpd.
Other traders also said that they expect Mitsubishi to strike a deal in the very near future, possibly on Friday.
Mitsubishi is acting as an agent for five Japanese oil companies, Japan Energy Corp (JOMO), Nippon Oil Co Ltd, Kashima Oil Co Ltd, Showa Shell Sekiyu KK and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd.
The deal, when concluded, will be the first between Iraq and a Japanese company under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
The contract must also be approved by the United Nations.

The United Nations said on Thursday that it had already approved five contracts under the deal which allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion-worth of oil over six months to pay for humanitarian goods for civilians suffering under sanctions.
Two of the contracts already approved were submitted by Turkish state oil concern TUPRAS and Coastal Corp of the United States.
TUPRAS is expected to lift about 75,000 bpd, while Coastal is expected to lift about 60,000 bpd of Iraqi crude.
Of the three other approved contracts, one is expected to have been the contract resubmitted by France's Elf Aquitaine . It was not accepted when it was first submitted due to a technical point.
Itochu Corp and Marubeni Corp have also sent staff to Baghdad, while Kanematsu Corp was thinking of sending a representative.

Japan was the single largest importer of Iraqi crude in Asia before 1990, importing about 200,000 bpd of the roughly 3.5 million bpd that Iraq produced prior to the U.N. sanctions. About 180,000 bpd were imported by Mitsubishi.
